brief.question: Build a simple, cross-platform desktop video editor driven by ffmpeg: drag and drop clips, alphabetical order that can be rearranged, any output format (mp4 default), choosable final picture size, split into N equal parts of the same quality, each part with its own max file size (default 20 MB), and a View Console option showing the ffmpeg commands as they run.
brief.purpose: New app built from the person's request; no target to study.
constraints: Linux, macOS and Windows; ffmpeg does the editing
brief.done_when: It builds, the --screenshot option saves a real picture, and a real export of mixed clips produces correct parts under their size limits.

handoff: Cutline now supports removing stretches: Mark start (I) / Mark end (O) at the playhead, Remove (X/Delete), Undo (Ctrl+Z), and red markers on the timeline that restore a cut when clicked. Cuts are stored per clip in source time (ClipItem.removed), so they follow a clip when it's reordered; plan::kept_ranges/merge_ranges feed Settings.removed, and the preview plays only the kept pieces. Verified: 21 unit + 8 real-FFmpeg tests, and a GUI run under Xvfb where a removed 8.4 s stretch gave a 19.6 s export from 28 s of clips. Shortcuts now use egui_wants_keyboard_input (focused() wrongly blocked Space after clicking the timeline). Windows/macOS still not run live.
